c.tagline: A clifftop Sicilian town with an ancient Greek theater framing views of smoking Mount Etna

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small shops and the beach cable car

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €4 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; parking is very limited so many visitors avoid driving into town

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: The historic center along Corso Umberto is pedestrian and very walkable; Isola Bella beach is reached by a cable car from town

safety.safety: Very safe town, popular with visitors of all ages
safety.crime: Petty theft in crowded areas during peak season is the main concern

hood_landmark.Corso Umberto (Historic Center): Corso Umberto's pedestrian shopping street and Piazza IX Aprile
hood_landmark.Teatro Antico Area: The Ancient Greek Theatre with its Etna backdrop
hood_landmark.Isola Bella: Isola Bella's nature reserve beach below town
hood_landmark.Castelmola: Castelmola's hilltop village and castle ruins
hood_landmark.Mazzarò: Mazzarò's harbor and cable car base

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing can occur in peak-season crowds on Corso Umberto and on buses and trains to/from the town.

hood_desc: The pedestrianized main street lined with boutiques, restaurants, and the clifftop Piazza IX Aprile terrace; the natural base for any visit.
The area around the ancient theater, still used for concerts and offering the town's most photographed Etna views.
A small nature reserve island and beach connected to the mainland by a sandbar, reached from town via cable car.
A dramatic hilltop village a short drive above Taormina, offering sweeping views back down at the coast.
The harbor and beach area below Taormina, connected by cable car, popular for swimming and boat trips.
lodging: San Domenico Palace, a Four Seasons Hotel
Mazzarò-Isola Bella cable car area lodging

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many prefer bottled for taste.

transit.sys: Interbus regional coaches and a cable car (funivia) linking the town to Mazzarò and Isola Bella beach
transit.pay: Tickets sold at the cable car station and bus kiosks
transit.note: The historic center is pedestrian; the cable car is the easiest way down to the beaches

transport.train: Taormina-Giardini train station on the coastal line, a short bus/taxi ride up to town
transport.bus: Interbus coaches connect to Catania, Messina, and the airport
transport.car: Reachable via the A18 motorway; parking in the historic center is very limited

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A TIM, Vodafone, or WindTre tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for tour guides
tip.r: A cover charge (coperto) is common instead of tipping; rounding up is a nice gesture
